answer: No. Micro-batch latency is the trigger interval plus the batch run time, so a 1 s trigger with a 1 s run gives a p50 near 1.5 s and a p99 near 2.5 s. That passes the median but misses the 2 s SLA on the tail, where trigger-based micro-batch loses. A 2 s SLA tolerates no trigger at all. Use a record-at-a-time engine (10 to 100 ms latency floor), such as the Rider ETA case in the lesson, even though the team prefers the batch engine.
